subject: Private Offer: BrightGrid — Rev-share & payment term exception request
messages:
From: markus_klein@redwood.ai
To: anna@brightgrid.com
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-04-19T09:12:00Z
Subject: Private Offer: BrightGrid — Rev-share & payment term exception request

Hi Anna,

Thanks again for the call this morning — great to see the BrightGrid team excited about moving ahead. Per our discussion, I've put together the private offer ask so we can get alignment before we submit to AWS Marketplace:

- Rev-share: BrightGrid is requesting a 28% rev-share on Marketplace billings for the first 12 months (you currently have a 20% baseline listed in the standard grid).
- Payment terms: customer is requesting net90 from Redwood.
- Upfront credit: customer has also requested a $200k upfront credit against first quarter usage.
- Marketplace listing: BrightGrid wants the offer live on AWS Marketplace (private listing) and needs the contract to reflect a specific revenue allocation for their resale partners.

This is a material deviation from standard deal desk guardrails (especially the rev-share and net90). Could you and Laura advise on whether we can escalate for exec consent and what the minimum acceptable concessions would be from our side? I'm including the SOW draft and a simple pricing waterfall for context.

Attachments: BrightGrid_SOW_v1.pdf, pricing_model.xlsx

Next steps I propose:
1) Quick internal review today (Karthik/Laura)
2) If needed, escalate to Marissa for conditional sign-off and finance/legal review
3) Present a revised private-offer term sheet to BrightGrid by Thursday EOD

Thanks,

—Markus Klein
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
From: anna@brightgrid.com
To: markus_klein@redwood.ai
Cc: legal@brightgrid.com
Date: 2028-04-19T10:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Private Offer: BrightGrid — Rev-share & payment term exception request

Markus,

Appreciate the quick summary and the docs. A couple clarifications from our side:

- The 28% rev-share is important to our commercial model because we have two resale partners that will each pull through a portion of usage; we need a higher floor for partner incentives.
- Net90 is non-negotiable for our procurement cadence — it's baked into our treasury plan for the year.
- The $200k upfront credit is flexible — we can split that into credits applied over two quarters if that helps.

If Redwood can commit to the higher rev-share and net90, we can lock a 24-month Private Offer term and a 2% commit-based uplift tied to usage thresholds.

Let me know what concessions you can make — happy to jump on a call after your internal alignment.

Best,
Anna Castillo
Head of Commercial Ops
BrightGrid

Marissa / Laura,

Looping you in per Markus' note. TL;DR of the ask: BrightGrid wants a temporary 28% rev-share (12 months), net90 payment terms, and a $200k upfront credit. They are willing to sign a 24-month private-offer and add a 2% commit-based uplift.

Assessment and suggested concessions:
- Rev-share: moving from 20% -> 28% is impactful; recommend offering a time-bound increase to 25% for 12 months with a clause to revert to baseline unless usage > $X/month. If exec approves, finance needs to sign off on revenue recognition impact.
- Payment terms: net90 is outside policy. Recommend compromise to net45 with a 60-day extension for first invoice only, or provide a 30-day holdback/credit mechanism instead of full net90. Finance favors net45 or risk-weighted escrow.
- Upfront credit: recommend splitting $200k into $100k upfront + $100k applied as committed usage credits across two quarters.

I have attached the SOW and pricing model. If Marissa can give conditional approval (exec-level) we can present the 25%/net45/$100k structure to BrightGrid and offer a 30-day run-rate review. If not, we should be prepared to hold firm on the rev-share.

Attachments: BrightGrid_SOW_v1.pdf, pricing_model.xlsx

Thanks,
Karthik
Director, Deal Desk
Redwood Inference

Team,

Thank you for the clear assessment. I can give conditional executive approval on the following limited concessions:

1) Rev-share: approve an elevated 25% rev-share for the first 12 months only, subject to a written clause that reverts to standard grid (20%) unless monthly net new usage > $150k for three consecutive months. Finance to confirm revenue impact and reporting cadence.
2) Payment terms: approve net45 standard. For the first invoice only, we will accept net60 if BrightGrid signs an ACH mandate and provides a 30% deposit on the initial commit.
3) Upfront credit: cap at $150k split as $100k upfront + $50k applied over two quarters; credit subject to clawback if usage thresholds are not met.

Action items:
- Laura: please coordinate with Legal to prepare the private-offer term sheet with the revert clause and clawback language.
- Karthik: get Finance (cc'ed) to confirm accounting treatment and prepare a short memo for bookings.
- Markus: present the revised offer to Anna by EOD Thursday and confirm their acceptance path (DocuSign + Marketplace listing process).

I want to be clear: this is a one-time concession tied to BrightGrid's strategic potential. Any extension beyond 12 months requires a post-mortem and formal exec renewal.

—Marissa Cole
Head of Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
